newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican Cetes rates march downwards on optimism.
newsitem.headline: Mexican Cetes rates march downwards on optimism.

text.p: Mexico's Cetes rates continued their decline on Tuesday at Banco de Mexico's weekly treasury bill auction, fueled by optimism over returns on the paper and easier money from the central bank, analysts said.
"The central bank gave the signal a week ago that it wanted lower rates, and I believe the market is still reacting," said Eduardo Estrada, an economist with Bancomer.
"I imagine that there is some optimism on the part of some investors, thinking about the returns (when converted) in dollars," he added.
Rates dropped more than expected across the yield curve at the auction. The benchmark one-month paper fell 206 basis points to 27.02 percent.
A Reuters' survey of 10 Cetes dealers earlier in the day had found expectations of a decline of 142 basis points to 27.66 percent in the 28-day term.
Last week, rates also fell more than expected after the central bank gave a signal that it was willing to allow easier monetary conditions.
The stable peso has allowed Banco de Mexico to sanction lower interest rates, analysts said.
The key one-month rates hit a recent high of 29.89 percent in mid-November as the peso ran into a patch of volatility.
But the one-month rate has fallen in the last three auctions, including this one.
Demand weakened to 12.81 billion pesos this week from 15.51 billion pesos last week, with most of the demand in the shorter-terms.

Mexican short-term paper has been gaining in popularity recently among foreign investors. Longer-term paper is less popular because of the anxiety about hotly contested mid-term elections in mid-1997.
Still, Mexico was the leading performer in November in JP Morgan's Emerging Local Markets Index (ELMI), released on Tuesday.

"Solid economic performance and falling inflation in Mexico prompted a peso rally, leading the country to reverse its October loss and become the month's best local emerging market performer, up 4.65 percent," JP Morgan said.

Analysts were also saying on Tuesday that funds from a recently redeemed $1.5 billion federal government note that allowed investors to take their returns in either pesos or U.S. dollars helped Mexican markets rally.
The rate on the three-month paper fell 164 basis points to 26.06 percent, while the six-month paper showed a decline of 128 basis points to 25.81 percent.
The yield on one-year paper was 25.46 percent this week compared with 26.50 percent the week before.
